subject: Ephemeral log erasure options and evidence for Orbis Analytics
messages:
From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@orbisanalytics.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: security@orbisanalytics.com
Date: 2026-12-08T16:14:00-05:00
Subject: Ephemeral logs / proof-of-delete options for tenant-scoped traces

Hi Vivek —

As part of our ongoing SIG/CAIQ review and SOC 2 evidence collection, our security team needs a clear description of Redwood's options for ephemeral debug/trace logs and the artifacts you can provide to prove deletion at the tenant scope. Specifically: 

1) For session/debug traces that are retained for 30 days (default in our eval), can Redwood provide a proof-of-delete manifest when records are purged? What does that manifest look like and does it include cryptographic hashes?
2) If we require a temporary legal hold for a subset of tenant traces (60 -> 180 days), what's the process and what approvals are needed? Will this be a signed addendum or can it be managed via the Console?
3) For customer-specific exceptions, what controls ensure other tenants' data is not affected (isolation/segmentation details)?

We'd like example artifacts we can ingest into our compliance tracker: deletion manifests, a short runbook for the deletion flow, and any SIG/SOC2 supporting snapshots. Can you share what you can produce and the expected turnaround?

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

Lydia Park
Head of Security, Orbis Analytics
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@orbisanalytics.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-08T17:02:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Ephemeral logs / proof-of-delete options for tenant-scoped traces

Lydia — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kimberly (Trust) and Priyom (Compliance) who own SIG/SOC2 artifacts and the deletion workflow. We can provide example manifests and a short runbook; a few clarifying notes up front: 

- Default ephemeral retention: session/debug traces are kept for 30 days by default and deleted via an automated job that produces a deletion manifest per-tenant. Manifests contain: tenant_id, timestamp, object_count, s3/object-store path prefixes, and an SHA256 of the concatenated object ids. We do not currently include per-file cryptographic hashes for every log chunk (we can provide an aggregated hash).
- Legal hold: temporary extensions are supported but require a signed customer addendum for retention beyond policy (we treat legal holds as an "exception" in our system). The Console will show hold state, but approval is done through our Compliance team and logged in the ticketing system.
- Isolation: erasure operations are scoped to tenant namespaces; the runtime enforces namespace-level access controls plus customer-scoped KMS keys for sensitive metadata.

Kimberly/Priyom — can you confirm attachments we can send today and whether an aggregated hash will satisfy Orbis for ingestion into their tracker? Also advise on typical turnaround. We aiming to get an artifact bundle to Lydia by end of week.

— Vivek
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@orbisanalytics.com>, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-09T09:18:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Ephemeral logs / proof-of-delete options for tenant-scoped traces

Hi Lydia, Vivek — thanks, quick answers and artifacts attached. Summary below followed by attachments.

Quick summary:
- Deletion manifest: per-tenant CSV with columns: tenant_id, deletion_time_utc, objects_deleted_count, prefix_path, aggregated_sha256, job_id. We attach a template: deletion-manifest-template.csv. The aggregated_sha256 is a hash over the manifest's object ids (deterministic ordering) and is sufficient for most compliance trackers.
- Runbook: tenant-erasure-runbook.pdf (attached) explains the automated job, retry/backoff, and manual recovery steps. It also describes controls that prevent cross-tenant deletes (namespace checks, KMS-wrapped keys on metadata objects).
- SIG/SOC2 artifacts: a one-page evidence summary (sig-evidence-summary.xlsx) showing where the artifacts map to SIG control IDs and where they are preserved in our evidence repository.

On legal holds/temporary extensions:
- Process: customer requests via support portal -> Compliance triage -> signed addendum for retention beyond standard TTL. Compliance maintains a hold ledger and triggers a non-delete flag so the automated job skips marked namespaces. The hold ledger export can be provided as a CSV for audit.
- Turnaround: standard requests are handled within 3 business days for assessment; after addendum, execution is immediate.

Next steps: I will drop the three attachments into the shared Drive link and send you a short verification checklist you can use when ingesting artifacts. If you need per-object hashes instead of aggregated hashes, we can scope an engineering task (timeline 2-3 weeks).

Attachments: tenant-erasure-runbook.pdf (runbook), deletion-manifest-template.csv (template), sig-evidence-summary.xlsx (mapping).

Best,
Kimberly Park
Security & Trust, Redwood Inference
From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@orbisanalytics.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-10T11:37:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Ephemeral logs / proof-of-delete options for tenant-scoped traces

Thanks — that's very helpful. A couple quick acceptance items from our side: 

1) The aggregated_sha256 approach is acceptable for initial ingestion, provided you include the job_id and deterministic ordering statement in the manifest (we want to be able to validate the hash reproducibly).
2) Please put the hold-ledger export format in the Drive link — we'll request an addendum template from Legal if the hold process is used.

If you can confirm the Drive link and push the artifacts there, we'll mark this as "evidence received" in our tracker and follow up with any minor clarifications. If the per-object-hash engineering option is chosen later, we'll log that as a security improvement request (SIR-241).

Appreciate the quick turn.

Lydia
Head of Security, Orbis Analytics
